newsitem.title: JAPAN: SESC files insider complaint vs Vitec - govt sources.
newsitem.headline: SESC files insider complaint vs Vitec - govt sources.

text.p: Japan's securities watchdog has filed insider trading complaints with prosecutors against Vitec Co Ltd, a former Vitec senior executive, and two related firms, government sources said Friday.

The Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) filed the complaints against Vitec, the firm's former president Kunihiro Konno, a real estate company he managed, and the firm that managed Vitec's assets, the sources said.
Vitec is a semiconductor trading firm affiliated to Sony Corp.
Government sources said Vitec bought 150,000 shares in Shintom Co Ltd from the market prior to a July 1994 announcement of a third-party allocation by the audio-visual equipment maker.
Vitec, which supplies Shintom with parts for its products, also provided capital for the establishment of a joint-venture firm by Shintom.
SESC launched a probe into the affair in October.
Vitec shares were traded on the over-the-counter market at 892 yen at midday Friday, compared to a 910 yen close on Thursday. Shintom had lost eight yen to 352 by midday.
